result.rationale:
TopicEmbed.import interpolates `url` unescaped into `contents << "\n
\n#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")}"` with only a `^https?://` regex check; quotes and angle brackets in a URL pass through. The content is then stored with cook_method raw_html (post.cooked == post.raw per the diff's own spec) and rendered unescaped via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, giving a stored-XSS injection path from feed/remote URLs. The mechanism is verifiable directly in the diff.

judged_text: The embed URL is interpolated unescaped into the imported_from footer (single-quoted href and bare text node) even though the only validation is the ^https?:// prefix check, so quotes and angle brackets pass through. A feed item link such as http://host/1'><script>alert(1)</script> injects markup into every rendered copy of the post (cooked is emitted raw), giving the feed author a second, independent stored-XSS path into the Discourse origin.

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the footer is built by interpolating the unescaped `url` into HTML: `I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")`, with only a `/^https?:\/\//` prefix check. This allows quotes/angle brackets in `url` (e.g. `http://host/1'>`) to break out of the single-quoted href and inject markup. The created post is explicitly marked `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` for that mode, and the embed view renders `raw post.cooked`, so the injected HTML would be stored and rendered without sanitization.
